items.title: The n-torsion of the Picard group of a smooth proper curve becomes the full standard group over a bounded separable extension
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file curves.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma makes the n-torsion of Picard visible over a finite separable extension with explicit degree bounds (statement lines 3642-3660). The proof (lines 3662-3695) chains: rational point over a bounded extension, torsion descent to k^{sep}, the continuous Galois action with open kernel, and the factorial degree bound from the permutation group cardinality; genus 1 reuses the same argument after existence of a rational point. The single omitted detail concerns the auxiliary remark that no uniform bound exists for g = 1, not the lemma's conclusions. H3: the Galois-descent orchestration with the quantitative bound is a genuine arithmetic argument.
